senses.gloss: A person who pretends to be something they are not.
examples: The man calling himself a surgeon turned out to be a *fake*.
She felt like a *fake* at her first big meeting.
Half the experts on that show are *fakes*.

senses.gloss: A quick move made to fool an opponent in a sport.
examples: He froze the defender with a *fake* and drove to the basket.
The quarterback's pump *fake* sent the safety the wrong way.
Her *fakes* are what make her so hard to guard.

senses.gloss: An act of dropping to the ground, usually by accident.
examples: She broke her wrist in a *fall* on the ice.
He took a bad *fall* off the ladder.
Most *falls* at home happen in the bathroom.

senses.gloss: A drop in the amount, level, or price of something.
examples: The report showed a sharp *fall* in unemployment.
A steady *fall* in prices hurt local growers.
*Falls* in temperature overnight can ruin the crop.

senses.gloss: The loss of power by a government, or the capture of a city.
examples: The class spent a week on the *fall* of the empire.
The *fall* of the city ended the war.
His *fall* from power took less than a month.

senses.gloss: The kind of story or film set in an imaginary world with magic.
examples: He reads nothing but *fantasy*.
The store keeps *fantasy* and science fiction on the same shelf.
It's a *fantasy* novel about a kingdom of dragons.

senses.gloss: The kind of food and drink served in a particular place.
examples: The menu is standard diner *fare*.
The festival offers everything from street *fare* to fine dining.
You'll find simple, hearty *fare* at that little cafe.

senses.gloss: A manner or way of doing something.
examples: The paperwork was filed in a timely *fashion*.
He answered every question in the same calm *fashion*.
The pieces came together in an odd *fashion*.

senses.gloss: The person who started or invented something important.
examples: Many people call him the *father* of modern computing.
The *father* of the theory died before anyone accepted it.
The ceremony honored the *fathers* of the space program.

senses.gloss: Weakening of metal or another material caused by repeated stress.
examples: The crack in the wing came from metal *fatigue*.
Inspectors look for signs of *fatigue* in the welds.
*Fatigue* in the old bridge cables worried the engineers.

senses.gloss: The plain, sturdy uniform that soldiers wear for work and training.
examples: He showed up in green *fatigues* and heavy boots.
The troops changed out of their *fatigues* before dinner.
She still keeps her old army *fatigues* in the closet.

senses.gloss: A kind act you do for someone because they asked.
examples: Can you do me a *favor* and watch the dog?
I owe him a *favor* after last week.
She's always asking for *favors* and never returning them.

senses.gloss: Approval or support for a person or an idea.
examples: The plan found *favor* with the city council.
That style has fallen out of *favor*.
He spent years trying to win the boss's *favor*.

senses.gloss: Food for farm animals or pets.
examples: We buy chicken *feed* by the fifty-pound bag.
The price of cattle *feed* went up again this spring.
He mixed the *feed* with a little warm water.

senses.gloss: Someone who buys stolen goods and sells them on.
examples: Detectives finally found the *fence* who moved the jewelry.
He worked as a *fence* out of a pawn shop.
Most of the *fences* in the city were under watch.

senses.gloss: Fences in general, or the material used to build them.
examples: We need another hundred feet of *fencing*.
The storm knocked down the *fencing* along the road.
Chain-link *fencing* runs around the whole lot.

senses.gloss: A state of intense excitement shared by many people.
examples: The whole town is in a *fever* over the playoffs.
Election *fever* took over the newsroom.
By June the excitement had reached a *fever* pitch.

senses.gloss: Something invented that people accept as if it were true.
examples: The idea that both sides agreed is a convenient *fiction*.
His entire resume turned out to be *fiction*.
The audit exposed the *fiction* behind the company's numbers.

senses.gloss: A subject or area of work that someone specializes in.
examples: She's a leading expert in her *field*.
The conference brings together people from several *fields*.
He left law for a *field* with better hours.

senses.gloss: A marked area of ground where a sport is played.
examples: The team took the *field* to a roar from the crowd.
Rain left the *field* too muddy to play on.
The high school built two new soccer *fields*.

senses.gloss: A space on a form or screen where you type one piece of information.
examples: Fill in every required *field* before you hit submit.
Leave the middle name *field* blank.
The database has separate *fields* for phone and email.

senses.gloss: The area in which a force such as magnetism or gravity acts.
examples: Iron filings show the shape of a magnetic *field*.
The satellite measures the earth's gravitational *field*.
Strong magnetic *fields* can wipe a hotel key card.

senses.gloss: Someone who fights in a boxing or martial arts contest.
examples: Both *fighters* made weight on Friday.
He's the most exciting *fighter* in the division.
The *fighter* wore his opponent down in the later rounds.

senses.gloss: A person who refuses to give up when things get hard.
examples: The doctors say she's a *fighter*.
He was a *fighter* right up to the end.
Kids who grow up like that turn into *fighters*.

senses.gloss: A tiny piece of metal rubbed off by a file or a saw.
examples: Iron *filings* lined up along the magnet.
Sweep the metal *filings* off the workbench.
A *filing* had worked its way into the gears.

senses.gloss: The work of putting documents in order and storing them.
examples: She spent the whole afternoon on *filing*.
*Filing* is the part of the job nobody wants.
There's a stack of *filing* sitting on my desk.

senses.gloss: Material or content added only to take up space or time.
examples: Half the article is *filler*.
That last episode was pure *filler*.
He told a long story as *filler* while the band set up.

senses.gloss: The hard material a dentist puts into a drilled tooth.
examples: I need a *filling* in one of my back teeth.
One of my old *fillings* fell out over the weekend.
The dentist replaced a silver *filling* with a white one.

senses.gloss: The thin strip of material used in a camera to record pictures.
examples: She still shoots on *film*.
He dropped off two rolls of *film* to be developed.
The old *film* had faded in the heat of the attic.

senses.gloss: An effect applied to a photo or video to change how it looks.
examples: She posted the picture with no *filter* at all.
That *filter* makes everything look like the seventies.
The app comes with dozens of *filters*.

senses.gloss: A program or setting that automatically blocks or sorts items.
examples: Your email must have landed in the spam *filter*.
Set a *filter* to show only orders from last month.
School computers have *filters* on most video sites.

senses.gloss: The last game of a competition, which decides the winner.
examples: They lost in the *final* by two points.
The *final* is on Sunday night.
She has reached three *finals* this season.

senses.gloss: The money that a person, company, or government has available.
examples: Our *finances* are tight this month.
The city's *finances* are in bad shape.
He hired someone to sort out his *finances*.

senses.gloss: The end of a race or contest, especially its closing stage.
examples: It was a photo *finish*.
The team faded badly in the *finish*.
He's known for a strong *finish* in the last mile.

senses.gloss: The shooting of guns.
examples: The patrol came under *fire* near the bridge.
The officers held their *fire*.
Heavy *fire* forced the crew to back away.

senses.gloss: A sudden short attack of illness, or a burst of strong feeling.
examples: She had a coughing *fit* in the middle of the meeting.
He threw a *fit* when he saw the bill.
The kids collapsed in *fits* of laughter.

senses.gloss: A small part used to join pipes or attach one thing to another.
examples: The leak was at the *fitting* under the sink.
He picked up a brass *fitting* at the hardware store.
All the *fittings* have to match the size of the pipe.

senses.gloss: An amount of something you feel you need on a regular basis.
examples: I need my morning coffee *fix* before I talk to anyone.
He gets his baseball *fix* on the radio.
Addicts will do almost anything for their next *fix*.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that has been part of a place so long they seem permanent.
examples: He's been a *fixture* at that diner for thirty years.
The old clock is a *fixture* of the town square.
Those two are *fixtures* on late-night television.

senses.gloss: A mark or warning put on something to show it needs attention.
examples: Missing paperwork like that is a red *flag*.
The system put a *flag* on his account.
The auditor raised several *flags* about the numbers.

senses.gloss: The side of a person's or animal's body between the ribs and the hip.
examples: The horse's *flanks* were dark with sweat.
He felt a sharp pain in his left *flank*.
She patted the cow's *flank* and stepped back.

senses.gloss: The far left or right side of an army, a team, or a formation.
examples: The enemy attacked on the left *flank*.
Their defense is weak on both *flanks*.
He sent riders out to protect the *flank*.

senses.gloss: A fashionable young woman of the 1920s who broke with older customs.
examples: She came to the party dressed as a *flapper*.
The photo shows two *flappers* with bobbed hair.
The novel follows a *flapper* through one long summer.

senses.gloss: A sudden burst of bright flame or light.
examples: A *flare* of orange lit up the window.
A solar *flare* knocked out radio signals for hours.
*Flares* of lightning showed the road ahead.

senses.gloss: The part of a camera that makes a bright light for a photograph.
examples: Turn off the *flash* inside the museum.
The *flash* went off right in my eyes.
Her camera's *flash* stopped working halfway through the party.

senses.gloss: A glass bottle with a wide base and a narrow neck, used in a laboratory.
examples: She heated the *flask* over a burner.
The liquid in the *flask* turned bright blue.
Rows of *flasks* lined the shelf above the sink.

senses.gloss: A tire that has lost its air.
examples: I got a *flat* on the way to work.
He changed the *flat* in the pouring rain.
Two *flats* in one month is terrible luck.

senses.gloss: An area of low, level ground, often muddy or salty.
examples: Birds feed on the mud *flats* at low tide.
They race cars out on the salt *flats*.
The *flats* below the highway flood every spring.

senses.gloss: All the vehicles, ships, or planes owned by one company or organization.
examples: The airline is replacing its aging *fleet*.
The company runs a *fleet* of delivery vans.
The city added twenty electric buses to its *fleet*.

senses.gloss: The soft part of a fruit or vegetable under the skin.
examples: The *flesh* of the melon was pale and sweet.
Scoop the *flesh* out of the avocado with a spoon.
Bake the squash until the *flesh* is soft.

senses.gloss: A movie (informal).
examples: We caught a *flick* on Saturday night.
It's a fun action *flick* with a silly ending.
He's seen every horror *flick* ever made.

senses.gloss: A trip made by airplane, or the plane making that trip.
examples: Our *flight* was delayed three hours.
She booked a *flight* home for the holidays.
All *flights* out of the airport were canceled.

senses.gloss: A set of stairs running between two floors or landings.
examples: Her apartment is up two *flights*.
He carried the boxes up a *flight* of stairs.
There's one more *flight* to the roof.

senses.gloss: The act of running away from danger.
examples: The war caused the *flight* of thousands of families.
Fear triggers the fight-or-*flight* response.
His sudden *flight* from the city surprised everyone.

senses.gloss: A long flat rubber shoe worn for swimming and diving.
examples: He pulled on his mask and *flippers*.
One *flipper* washed up on the beach a day later.
*Flippers* make you much faster in the water.

senses.gloss: A drink made of soda with ice cream floating in it.
examples: He ordered a root beer *float*.
The diner on Main Street makes great *floats*.
A *float* is just soda and a scoop of vanilla.

senses.gloss: A small object on a fishing line that rests on the surface and dips when a fish bites.
examples: Watch the *float* — it just went under.
He clipped a red and white *float* onto the line.
The *floats* bobbed in the current all afternoon.

senses.gloss: A very large number of things arriving at the same time.
examples: The station got a *flood* of calls after the story aired.
A *flood* of applications came in overnight.
She faced *floods* of questions from reporters.

senses.gloss: The ground at the bottom of the ocean, a forest, or a valley.
examples: Strange creatures live on the ocean *floor*.
Fallen leaves cover the forest *floor*.
The valley *floor* is the best farmland around.

senses.gloss: The lowest level that a price or amount is allowed to fall to.
examples: The law sets a *floor* under wages.
Traders think the market has finally found a *floor*.
There's a price *floor* for milk.

senses.gloss: The part of a legislature or meeting where members speak and vote.
examples: The bill finally reached the *floor*.
The senator asked for the *floor*.
Debate on the *floor* lasted six hours.

senses.gloss: A sudden short burst of activity.
examples: There was a *flurry* of calls right before closing.
The announcement set off a *flurry* of trading.
After a few early *flurries*, the day went quiet.

senses.gloss: A tall narrow glass with a stem, used for champagne.
examples: The waiter handed each guest a *flute* of champagne.
They got a set of crystal *flutes* as a wedding gift.
He raised his *flute* for the toast.

senses.gloss: A state of constant change.
examples: The schedule is still in *flux*.
The whole industry is in a state of *flux*.
Prices have been in *flux* all year.

senses.gloss: The opening at the front of a pair of pants, closed with a zipper or buttons.
examples: Your *fly* is open.
The zipper on his *fly* broke on the way to work.
These jeans have a button *fly*.

senses.gloss: An artificial bait made to look like an insect, used in fishing.
examples: He ties his own *flies* all winter.
She cast a small dry *fly* upstream.
That *fly* has caught more trout than anything else in my box.

senses.gloss: Material used up for some purpose, especially to feed talk or criticism.
examples: The scandal was perfect *fodder* for late-night comedians.
His private life became tabloid *fodder*.
The leaked memo gave his critics plenty of *fodder*.

senses.gloss: A state of confusion in which you cannot think clearly.
examples: I got through the whole week in a *fog*.
The medication left her in a mental *fog*.
The first months after the baby were a complete *fog*.

senses.gloss: A person or thing whose differences make another's qualities stand out.
examples: The quiet brother is a *foil* for the loud one.
Her calm serves as a *foil* to his temper.
Every hero in the book has a *foil*.

senses.gloss: A light sword with a thin blade, used in fencing.
examples: She competes with the *foil*.
He raised his *foil* and saluted his opponent.
The rack held a dozen *foils* and masks.

senses.gloss: People in general, or the people of a particular place.
examples: *Folks* around here are pretty friendly.
A lot of *folks* showed up for the meeting.
Most *folks* never read the fine print.

senses.gloss: Your parents, or your close family.
examples: My *folks* live a few hours north of here.
We're spending the holidays with her *folks*.
His *folks* helped him buy the truck.
